# A free Fisher unit ball gives a finite affine design operation

30 October 2026. Governing completed construction. The inherited conditional-Umegaki/free-Fisher theorem is an accepted programme input; the linear-pencil reduction below is proved here. Execution, prior, cost and version-bound independent review are separate receipts. No physical calibration, privacy, guessing or multi-use claim is made.

## 1. Scope and reusable input

Let L be a strictly entrywise positive, column-stochastic ell-by-n classical channel, n>=2. Its shape and rank are arbitrary. Let K be an m-by-n column-stochastic channel, with an imposed rational entry floor 0<kappa<1/m. The floor is useful for design and uniform inverse denominators; it can be arbitrarily small. The budget c is nonnegative. Both channels share the SAME explicitly classical input boundary.

For classical-quantum hypotheses and any finite complex reference R, write

    J_A(rho,sigma) = D((A tensor id)rho || (A tensor id)sigma)
                    - D(rho_R || sigma_R).

Only finite differences are defined. This is a SUBTRACTED/conditional comparison, equivalently the equal-reference-marginal comparison. It is NOT the uncentered all-reference inequality D_K<=c D_L: identical reference information forces c>=1 in that different task. The accepted input theorem in sol24/c_independent_opening/source_entry/FREE_UMEGAKI_PROOF.md says J_K<=c J_L for all finite references iff

    F_K(Q,u) <= c F_L(Q,u),                                  (1)
    F_A(Q,u) = sum_y (A u)_y^* (A Q)_y^{-1} (A u)_y,
    Q_i>=0, sum_i Q_i=I, sum_i u_i=0.

Here u_i are complex vectors and (AQ)_y=sum_i A_yi Q_i. Positivity of every channel entry makes all inverse denominators positive, including boundary effects Q_i=0. The faithful-Q and closed-Q versions agree by mixing each Q_i with I/n and continuity. This proof starts from (1), rather than reopening that inherited theorem.

The output of the construction is ONE finite SDP, affine jointly in unknown K and c, whose feasibility is EXACTLY (1). For a fixed positive budget and floor, linear utility design has a rational strictly feasible certificate, a bounded feasible set, and polynomial weak-optimization complexity with the usual explicit bit/accuracy inputs. Exact threshold decision at a boundary and practical solver speed are separate claims.

## 2. Operatorization and the unit-ball equivalence

Replace vectors u_i by arbitrary operators U_i on the reference space, still with sum_i U_i=0. Define the operator-valued quadratic form

    F_A(Q,U) = sum_y (A U)_y^* (A Q)_y^{-1} (A U)_y.

The vector inequality (1) implies this operator inequality: test any vector xi and put u_i=U_i xi. Conversely every vector tuple is represented by rank-one U_i=u_i e^* for a unit e, so the two universal assertions are equivalent. U_i need NOT be Hermitian.

Consider the Hermitian pencils

    A_L(Q,U) = diag(Q_1,...,Q_n)
                 direct_sum [ diag((LQ)_1,...,(LQ)_ell)   LU ],
                            [             (LU)^*          I  ]

    B_K,c(Q,U) = [ diag((KQ)_1,...,(KQ)_m)   KU ].          (2)
                [            (KU)^*          c I ]

The LU and KU blocks are block columns. Their scalar coefficient sizes are e=n+ell+1 and f=m+1. Source positivity means precisely Q_i>=0 and F_L(Q,U)<=I; target positivity means F_K(Q,U)<=c I. Therefore (1) implies free pencil inclusion A_L>=0 => B_K,c>=0.

For the converse fix any Q,U and eps>0 and set T=(F_L(Q,U)+eps I)^(-1/2), U'_i=U_i T. Then sum U'_i=0 and

    F_L(Q,U')=T^* F_L(Q,U) T <= I.

Inclusion yields T^* F_K(Q,U) T<=c I. Congruence by T^{-1} gives F_K(Q,U)<=c(F_L(Q,U)+eps I). Let eps decrease to zero. This is valid even if F_L is singular or zero. In particular it introduces no inverse of L, no fixed-rank quotient and no nonexistent inverse on a null tangent.

## 3. Fixed coefficient matrices

Use 3(n-1) independent selfadjoint free variables X_j,Y_j,Z_j, j<n:

    Q_j=I/n+X_j,        Q_n=I/n-sum_{j<n}X_j,
    U_j=Y_j+i Z_j,      U_n=-sum_{j<n}(Y_j+i Z_j).

Then A=A0+sum_j A_j x_j and B=B0+sum_j B_j x_j are Hermitian affine pencils. All A coefficients are FIXED by L. All B coefficients are AFFINE in K and c. Specifically A0 is diagonal with n entries 1/n, then the ell row means s_z=(sum_i L_zi)/n, then 1. Hence

    A0>0,   Tr A0=3,   Tr A_j=0 for every nonconstant j.     (3)

The X_j diagonal coefficients are +1 on Q_j, -1 on Q_n and L_zj-L_zn on reference row z. The Y_j coefficient has L_zj-L_zn in the (z,last) and (last,z) source-block positions. The Z_j coefficient has i(L_zj-L_zn) above and -i(L_zj-L_zn) below. Target coefficients have the same last two patterns with K, and the X_j diagonals K_yj-K_yn. B0=diag(rowmeans(K),c).

Rank deficiency leaves some U directions unbounded in the source domain. No boundedness premise will be imposed to hide them. If h is in ker L, column stochasticity implies sum h_i=0. Substituting U_i=h_i T into (1) forces K h=0 for any finite c. The SDP below therefore enforces the necessary K ker L=0 gate automatically.

## 4. Exact linear free Farkas lemma, including unbounded domains

The following is ordinary free-linear Positivstellensatz machinery, with a short proof to pay the complex and unbounded-domain conventions. Let A(x)=A0+sum_{j=1}^g A_j x_j have Hermitian e-by-e coefficients and A0>0. Let B(x) have Hermitian f-by-f coefficients. Then positivity of B on every finite complex matrix level of {A>=0} is equivalent to

    B0=R+Phi(A0),  B_j=Phi(A_j),  R>=0, Phi completely positive.  (4)

Write the Choi matrix C=[C_ab]_{a,b=1}^e, C_ab=Phi(E_ab), C>=0. Then Phi(A)=sum_ab A_ab C_ab. Sufficiency is immediate by the Kraus representation and R>=0.

For necessity consider the cone of coefficient tuples given by (4). It is CLOSED: for any convergent tuple B^(r), positivity of A0 and the constant identity imply

    lambda_min(A0) Tr C^(r) + Tr R^(r) <= Tr B0^(r).

Thus C^(r),R^(r) are bounded PSD matrices and have convergent subsequences. If B is not in the cone, a real separating functional has Hermitian matrices Y_0,...,Y_g such that

    sum_j Tr(Y_j B_j)<0,
    Y0>=0,   W=sum_{j=0}^g A_j^T tensor Y_j>=0.             (5)

The transpose is important: it follows by expanding Tr(W C). Choose sufficiently small eps>0 so the first inequality remains negative after Y0 is replaced by Y0+eps I. Then W+eps A0^T tensor I is PSD. Put S=[(Y0+eps I)^T]^(1/2) and X_j=S^{-1}Y_j^T S^{-1}. Full transpose of W followed by congruence gives A(X)>=0 at matrix size f. With Omega=sum_{a=1}^f e_a tensor e_a and v=(I_f tensor S)Omega,

    v^* B(X) v = Tr[(Y0+eps I)B0]+sum_{j>=1}Tr(Y_j B_j)<0.

This contradicts inclusion. There is no compactness assumption on the SOURCE spectrahedron. The only compactness used is the bounded Choi/R certificate sequence furnished by A0>0. The proof also yields a violating matrix tuple of size at most f if inclusion fails.

Helton-Klep-McCullough (2012), Theorem1.1 and Section4.1, are controlling primary antecedents for this d=0 positivity/CP machinery. Their non-strict convex Positivstellensatz explicitly does not require boundedness. The proof above supplies the exact complex coefficient/transposition convention used here; it is not a new generic free Farkas theorem.

## 5. The general synthesis SDP

Combine Sections1-4. The exact feasible set is the projection of

    C>=0 of order (n+ell+1)(m+1),
    R>=0 of order m+1,
    Phi_C(A0)+R=B0(K,c),
    Phi_C(A_j)=B_j(K) for 1<=j<=3(n-1),
    sum_y K_yi=1,   K_yi>=kappa,   c>=0.                   (6)

Every equality is AFFINE JOINTLY in K,c,C,R. Thus the square inverse is removed for all positive rectangular/rank-deficient references; this is not a hierarchy or a finite-witness optimization with an unbounded hidden cutoff. The Choi variable certifies a map between pencil coefficient algebras. It is NOT a postprocessing channel from L outputs to K outputs, and (6) does not claim a physical degrader.

Although A_Z and B_Z are imaginary Hermitian, an exact REAL symmetric Choi/R realization suffices. Strip the common i from every Z equation, leaving real skew matrices. All equations now have real coefficients. If a complex Hermitian solution exists, its entrywise conjugate also solves these stripped equations; average them. The result is real symmetric and PSD, and reinstating i recovers every complex equation. Both symmetric and skew coefficient equalities must be enforced: dropping the skew equations would silently lose arbitrary complex references.

The semidefinite orders and number of equality entries are polynomial in n,ell,m. The certificate is exact for any c>=0. Positivity floors and c upper bounds are separate linear constraints rather than rational denominators.

## 6. Paid weak-SDP complexity

For fixed rational 0<c and 0<kappa<1/m, take K0_yi=1/m. Let

    eta=min(1/m,c)/6,    C0=eta I_(ef),
    R0=diag(1/m,...,1/m,c)-3 eta I_f.

All nonconstant coefficient matches vanish by (3). C0,R0 and the K entry slacks are strictly positive with rational polynomial-bit margins. This is an explicit strictly feasible point in the affine equality space, regardless of rank(L). If c is an optimized variable in [0,cmax] with rational cmax>0, use c0=cmax/2 and include its two scalar slacks; the same construction is strict. The c=0 constant-release boundary is included by the exact SDP, without claiming a strict c=0 certificate.

Let a0=min{1/n, min_z s_z,1}>0. From the constant match, for any feasible point with c<=cmax,

    Tr C <= (1+cmax)/a0,   Tr R<=1+cmax.                    (7)

The stochastic K and bounded c also have explicit norm bounds. Represent the PSD blocks and all scalar inequality slacks as one block-diagonal SDP variable. The baseline's smallest displayed slack is an explicit inner radius for a Frobenius ball IN THE AFFINE EQUALITY SPACE (take half the smallest slack); all block entries are affine coordinates, so no unknown condition number is required. Polynomial-bit Gaussian elimination can remove dependent equality rows. Equations(3),(7) give rational outer-radius bounds about that baseline. Hence the usual rational weak-SDP theorem (deKlerk-Vallentin, Theorem1.1) applies, with cost polynomial in alphabet sizes, rational input bit lengths and log(1/accuracy). This does not assert exact boundary decision, strongly polynomial runtime, a practical speedup over all source-aware methods, or cheap physical qualification.

## 7. Scope retained

The new interface starts from a supplied classical L, raw classical input X, a specified linear utility/cost and a justified one-use conditional-information contract. It does not acquire L from samples, give raw X to an observer who only has L(X), implement a quantum reference experiment, or amplify the one-use budget into correlated multi-use compression. References may be arbitrary and noncommuting in the guarantee, but no reference needs to be sampled by the compiler.

The general free-linear inclusion theorem was already available. The substantive representation is the Fisher UNIT BALL that exposes a small affine source pencil; ordinary SDP machinery then does the synthesis. Priority is UNKNOWN. The same-information ordinary route includes this construction once its reduction is known, binary scalar Fisher optimization when applicable, general rational free positivity and exact real-algebraic methods. Actual numerical/exact receiver results and their costs will be reported without demoting those incumbents.

## 8. Boundary channels: the same finite operation covers every classical L

Strict entrywise positivity can be removed, with an explicit boundary convention. Let L be ANY finite nonnegative column-stochastic reference, delete its identically zero output rows, and keep its remaining ell rows. Let K also be merely nonnegative column-stochastic; identically zero rows contribute zero to F_K. The accepted inherited free formula is stated for exactly these nonzero-output-row channels, with faithful Q_i>0. Every W_y of a nonzero row is then positive definite. A0 in Section3 is still positive definite because each remaining row mean is positive. Thus all coefficient construction, closed-cone proof and trace bounds remain unchanged.

To prove the inclusion reduction without inverting any singular boundary W, first work only with faithful Q. Schur complements apply to all nonzero rows; a zero K row has both W_y=0 and (KU)_y=0 and can be deleted from that block test. The right-normalization proof remains valid. It establishes target positivity at every source-feasible point with faithful Q. For an arbitrary boundary source-feasible tuple x, replace x by (1-delta)x. Its source pencil is

    A((1-delta)x)=(1-delta)A(x)+delta A0>0,

and every Q_i has the added delta I/n. Target positivity at these tuples and continuity give B(x)>=0. This pays the closure in the needed direction and never substitutes an inverse on a null boundary support. Conversely free inclusion immediately bounds the faithful-Q forms and invokes the same inherited theorem.

Consequently (6) covers arbitrary finite classical reference channels, including their zero entries, rectangular shapes and rank deficiency. K may be constrained by any 0<=kappa<1/m, including kappa=0. The strictly positive constant baseline still supplies all scalar K slacks at kappa=0. Nonzero reference row means give polynomial-bit a0 from rational input; deleting zero rows is exact rational preprocessing. Actual execution below uses a strictly positive tall source, so this boundary extension is analytic and not a separate executed boundary-channel case.

# From a rational angular identity to full strong quasiconvexity

30 October 2026. Root's independent quantitative reconstruction for A's
original quartic. This supplies an analytical receiver for a LITERAL
polynomial identity/PSD certificate. It does not certify those premise
bytes, historical novelty or the target's non-polyconvexity by itself.
Those are separate source/certificate obligations being challenged by T.

Let F be the actual homogeneous quartic on2-by-2 matrices, A=(a,b,c,d)
in row order, T=|A|^2. Let alpha=P5(A)/T on A!=0, for a polynomial1-form
P5 homogeneous of degree5, extended by0 at0. Let omega=dalpha. For any
compatible second jet h=(u1_xx,u1_xy,u1_yy,u2_xx,u2_xy,u2_yy), put

 B1=(h0,h1,h3,h4), B2=(h1,h2,h4,h5),
 J(a,b,c,d)=(-c,-d,a,b),
 D=F''(A)[B1,B1]+F''(A)[B2,B2]
       +nu(F''(A)[B1,JB2]+F''(A)[B2,JB1]).

Assume the exact certificate proves

 T^2 [D+omega_A(B1,B2)]=z(A,h)^T Q z(A,h),
 Q>=I/2000, |nu|<1/1000,                              (1)

where z lists EACH degree3 monomial in the four A entries times EACH of
the six h entries, exactly once. These are the concrete symbolic premises,
not an optimization-status or finite-grid substitute.

## 1. The origin and the null integral

alpha is smooth off0 and homogeneous degree3. On the unit sphere all its
derivatives are bounded. Its derivatives of orders0,1,2 consequently scale
as |A|^3,|A|^2,|A| and extend continuously by0 at the origin. Successive
difference quotients show these are the actual derivatives there. Hence
alpha is C^2 globally, omega is C^1, homogeneous degree2, and its pullback
under every smooth periodic A is an exact2-form. Stokes gives

    integral omega_A(partial_x A,partial_y A)=0.

No third derivative at0, analytic extension or punctured-domain boundary
term is silently assumed. Smooth approximation of alpha also gives the
same pullback identity if desired.

## 2. A genuinely smoothing compatible-gradient flow

For arbitrary constant M and smooth periodic phi:T^2->R^2, evolve

    phi_t=Delta phi+2nu J2 phi_xy,
    J2=[[0,-1],[1,0]], A=M+Dphi.

On Fourier mode k its propagator is heat decay exp(-|k|^2 t) times a
real orthogonal rotation exp(-2nu kx ky J2 t). Thus the solution remains
smooth and periodic, A is always a compatible gradient, and A->M smoothly
as t->infinity. A scalar positive heat kernel is unnecessary. Normalizations
for a2pi-periodic torus only change the Fourier notation.

Integration by parts gives

    d/dt integral F(A)=-integral D.

The two cross terms have identical INTEGRALS, since each arises by
integrating DF(A).J partial_xy A along one of the two coordinates. No
pointwise identity of those cross terms is required. Adding the Stokes
integrand leaves this energy derivative unchanged.

Every multinomial coefficient in T^3 is at most6. Therefore

 D+omega_A(B1,B2)>=T |h|^2/12000.

Because |DA|^2=|B1|^2+|B2|^2<=2|h|^2, the F energy gap is at least

therefore gives

 integral G(M+Dphi)-G(M)
 <=12(1+|nu|) integral_0^infinity integral |A|^2|DA|^2.  (3)

Pointwise uniform convexity gives
G(M+v)-G(M)-DG(M).v>=|v|^4/3. For |v|=1 the minimum occurs at
M=-(1/3)v, with no perpendicular component; scaling proves the general
case. The linear term integrates to0 for periodic gradients. Combining
(2),(3) proves

 integral [F(M+Dphi)-F(M)]
 >= [864000(1+|nu|)]^-1 integral |Dphi|^4
 >= (1/900000) integral |Dphi|^4.                     (4)

The bounds themselves imply finiteness of the required integrals; one can

For a smooth compactly supported variation on an arbitrary bounded open
domain, extend it by0 into a larger rectangular periodic cell. The outside

# Matching rare-transport law for the conserving common-clock family

29 October 2026. Root follow-on receiving theorem. This closes the
scalar lower-bound gap left by the earlier common-clock upper bound,
at an explicitly warranted canonical initial law. It does not prove
the proposed full nonlocal density/current action.

## 1. Result and actual initialization

Use the even-N conserving ring

    r_i=c(1+alpha u delta_i), c=s/2, 0<alpha<1,
    u=sigma p(eta), p=(-1)^(sum_i i eta_i),
    delta_i=eta_i-eta_(i+1), A=sum_i delta_i^2.           (1)

One actual common Poisson clock flips sigma at physical rate gamma_N,
with gamma_N->infinity and gamma_N/N->0. Initialize occupancies from
the uniform canonical law with exactly M_N particles, M_N/N->m in
(0,1), and initialize sigma independently and fairly. Denote this
stationary joint law by mu_N. It is an actual initial-law premise;
this theorem does not supply its preparation or erase its retained
records. Conditional use requires that law, or the explicit additional
initial entropy condition discussed below, and the complete declared
future native-and-clock generator.

For Q_N=J(N^2T)/N^2, the scalar LDP at speed N has rate

    I_T^common(q)=q^2/[2s chi(m)(1-alpha^2)T].            (2)

Its scaled cumulant generating function is

    lim_N N^-1 log E exp[N lambda Q_N]
       =(s/2)chi(m)(1-alpha^2)T lambda^2.                (3)

The existing upper bound holds even for arbitrary deterministic
initial occupancies of the same asymptotic mass. The new lower proof
here is canonical-initial; it does not silently extend that upper
bound to a matching deterministic-initial theorem.

For a matched common/independent comparison, use this same canonical
visible law and record every initial orientation as +1. The common
initial relative entropy against mu_N is then only log2, so the proof
below still applies. For independent controls, the scalar reference
proof also applies to this random initial visible law: its upper
bound uses only the conserved mass, and its weak-tilt lower receiver
needs initial empirical convergence in probability to the flat profile,
which the canonical law supplies. The same uniform phase/occupation
estimates and martingale identification establish that receiver.
Thus the two scalar rates can be compared with the same actual start.
This observation does not give a fixed-initial-profile full spatial
action to a randomly initialized canonical ensemble; its full spatial
LDP would also have to carry the initial density's static cost.

## 2. The corrected-current comparison has an unusually small adjoint source

On active native bonds define d_i=delta_i-alpha u; set d_i=0 on
inactive bonds, which do not produce events. Let M be the sum of d_i
over native events. The preceding exact construction gives

    sum_i r_i d_i=0,
    sum_i r_i d_i^2=c(1-alpha^2)A.                      (4)

Both r_i and the reference law are invariant under their own native
swap, whereas d_i changes sign. For a fixed real lambda define a
mathematical comparison generator by native rates

    r_i^lambda=r_i exp(lambda d_i/N),                   (5)

with the same common clock. No physical actuator for (5) is assumed.
On macroscopic time its adjoint, with respect to mu_N, satisfies

    (L_N^lambda)^*1
       =-2N^2 sum_i r_i sinh(lambda d_i/N).             (6)

The linear term vanishes exactly by (4). Since |d_i|<=2 and the
total native rate is at most cN, the cubic remainder gives

    ||(L_N^lambda)^*1||_infinity<=C_(lambda,c),          (7)

uniformly in N and gamma_N. A generic weak tilt has an O(N) form
cost; this particular corrected-current tilt has an O(1) adjoint
source. That cancellation is the useful additional connection.

## 3. Entropy controls the needed activity under the comparison law

Let f_t be the density of the comparison law relative to mu_N.
It starts at one. The elementary inequality log y-log x<=y/x-1,
applied to the finite-state jump generator, yields

    d/dt H(f_t mu_N | mu_N)
       =int f_t L_N^lambda log f_t dmu_N
       <=int f_t (L_N^lambda)^*1 dmu_N
       <=C_(lambda,c).                                (8)

Thus the entropy is bounded by C_(lambda,c)T on the full macroscopic
interval. Under mu_N the canonical activity satisfies

    E[A/N]=2m_N(1-m_N)N/(N-1), Var(A/N)=O(1/N).         (9)

For a fixed delta>0, Chebyshev gives a reference bad-event probability
O(1/N). The entropy event inequality

    nu(B)<= [H(nu|mu)+log2]/log[1/mu(B)]                (10)

then makes the comparison bad-event probability tend to zero,
uniformly for t<=T. Since 0<=A/N<=1, integration in time gives

    int_0^T A(eta_(N^2t))/N dt -> 2chi(m)T
                                    in P^lambda probability.    (11)

Only canonical finite-space moments and the O(1) entropy source were
needed. No complete common-clock hydrodynamic theorem was imported.
The same proof permits an initial relative entropy o(log N) against
mu_N using (9)--(10), if it is actually warranted. Stronger initial
entropy classes would require a stated stronger concentration bound;
they are not needed for the displayed theorem.

## 4. Typical corrected current and likelihood cost

Under (5), the scaled corrected current M(N^2t)/N^2 has a martingale
part of bracket O(1/N), and its drift is

    sum_i r_i exp(lambda d_i/N)d_i
       =[lambda c(1-alpha^2)/N]A+O_lambda(N^-1).        (12)

The remainder follows from bounded d_i and sum r_i=O(N). Hence (11)
implies

    M(N^2T)/N^2 -> v_alpha lambda,
    v_alpha=s chi(m)(1-alpha^2)T.                      (13)

The exact correction between Q_N and M/N^2 is superexponentially
negligible under the original law, as already proved. The likelihood
for (5) is a bounded weak tilt, |lambda d_i/N|<=2|lambda|/N. Its
second-moment identity therefore transfers that negligible event to
the comparison law. In particular Q_N has the same limit (13).

The likelihood is exactly

    Z_lambda=exp[lambda M/N-B_N(lambda)],
    B_N=int_0^(N^2T)sum_i r_i
          [exp(lambda d_i/N)-1-lambda d_i/N]dv.          (14)

The omitted linear compensator is identically zero by (4). Equations
(4) and (11) give B_N/N -> v_alpha lambda^2/2 in comparison probability.
Together with (13),

    N^-1 log Z_lambda -> v_alpha lambda^2/2.            (15)

Choose lambda=q/v_alpha. On a comparison-typical event with Q_N near
q and likelihood cost near I_T^common(q), restrict
P(B)=E^lambda[Z_lambda^-1 1_B]. This yields the lower exponent
-I_T^common(q). The existing local upper bound and exponential
tightness yield the full scalar LDP (2).

## 5. Exponential moments and the closed-gate limit

The bounded-jump martingale estimate gives a finite O(N) log-moment
bound for M/N at every fixed multiplier. In the exact correction for
Q_N, the common-clock martingale and its occupation integral each
cost only O(gamma_N) in fixed speed-N exponential moments under mu_N.
Holder's inequality therefore gives finite speed-N moment envelopes
at every multiplier for Q_N. Combining those envelopes at 2lambda
with exponential tightness supplies the exponential-integrability
tail condition. The LDP Laplace principle proves (3), not just a
formal Legendre calculation.

If instead alpha_N->1, including alpha_N=1 exactly, the existing
superexponential circulation suppression gives the degenerate rate
zero at q=0 and infinity elsewhere. Under the stated stationary law,
the same moment bounds have divided log costs bounded by
C_lambda[(1-alpha_N^2)+gamma_N/N+1/N], which vanish. The scaled
cumulant generating function is therefore zero; Jensen supplies the
matching lower bound since stationary mean current is zero.

The full shared-clock spatial action and deterministic-initial
matching lower bound remain open. The completed result already shows
that altering joint control correlations, at identical marginal
per-bond clock rates, can change a real rare-transport law within this
constructed reversible family. The independent/grouped fast-control
theorem supplies the reference law, while the present common-clock
regime supplies (2) or the closed-gate limit.

# Normally displayed final: formula text projection

Deterministic text projection of the normally displayed final, preserving its mathematical annotations. This is not an acquired original proof, implementation, or independent review document. Raw visible text and private formula DOM are preserved separately.

I developed a constructive route to exact averaged Petz recovery from forward experiments, and obtained a stronger limitation on the entire classical-compilation programme: its dimension-and-noise cost cannot generally be amortized across a batch.

The central construction is positive matrix debiasing: correct the statistical bias of an experimentally acquired instruction while ensuring that every instruction actually executed is a valid quantum channel. The accompanying resource result is $\boxed{
\sup_{\mathcal E:\,J_{\mathcal E}\succeq \nu I/d^2}
\mathbb E_{\mathcal E}T
\;\ge\;
M\left(1+\frac d\nu\right).
}$ 

That bound applies to exact reproduction acquired through separately measured source outputs, even when the resulting classical programs are correlated and their execution can prepare entangled batch outputs.

These are completed local mathematical constructions with separate internal checks. External acceptance and comprehensive priority review remain open. The general recovery compiler has not been physically implemented.

1. The selected investigation: execute a nonlinear recovery operation

I chose a stronger target than reproducing the forward channel: acquire, using forward experiments, a classical instruction whose average implements its Petz recovery channel relative to a supplied faithful prior  $\sigma$ .

Writing  $\tau=\mathcal E(\sigma)$ , the target is $\mathcal R_{\sigma,\mathcal E}(Y)
=
\sigma^{1/2}
\mathcal E^\dagger
\!\left(
\tau^{-1/2}Y\tau^{-1/2}
\right)
\sigma^{1/2}.$ 

This is a standard recovery operation. Existing implementation work includes algorithms using block encodings and access to a Stinespring unitary for the source channel and its inverse. Those are materially stronger controls than ordinary forward input/output experiments. arxiv.org

The investigated interface is:

The source is an unknown, fixed, memoryless channel with the supplied Choi floor.

Acquisition uses known inputs and fresh output measurements.

Only a classical instruction survives acquisition.

A supplied trusted catalogue implements the selected known channel.

The later payload may be unknown and entangled with a reference.

Exactness averages the current instruction and acquisition record. Independent future uses require independent instructions.

The construction targets the whole recovery channel. Checking only that it returns the known prior would be insufficient: a device that simply prepares  $\sigma$  could pass that test.

Also, Petz recovery is not an inverse that restores arbitrary states after arbitrary noise. The operation itself is implemented exactly in the mathematical average; its recovery performance remains the performance of the Petz map.

Why the previous factory does not immediately solve this

From $\mathbb E[\Gamma_V]=\mathcal E$ 

one generally cannot conclude $\mathbb E[\mathcal R_{\sigma,\Gamma_V}]
=
\mathcal R_{\sigma,\mathcal E}.$ 

The inverse square root makes the target nonlinear. Applying a recovery formula separately to the old random instructions therefore does not establish the desired operation.

The new construction addresses that bias directly.

2. Central mechanism: physical corrections whose mean telescopes

Let  $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)$  denote probabilities of informationally complete ordinary source experiments. Let  $F(p)$  be the normalized Choi matrix of the desired operation.

The sufficient theorem uses a computable  $C^4$  extension $F:[0,1]^m\longrightarrow\{\text{normalized channel Choi matrices}\}$ 

with a known uniform interior margin $F(q)\succeq \kappa\,\frac{I}{d^2}.$ 

The extension over the entire probability cube is necessary: empirical frequencies need not themselves describe a physical channel.

Correct the leading sampling bias

Define $G(q)=\sum_i q_i(1-q_i)\,\partial_{ii}F(q),
\qquad
H_n(q)=F(q)-\frac{G(q)}{2n}.$ 

After acquiring  $2n$  observations of each experiment, let  $k$  be the vector of total counts. The distribution of counts in a uniformly selected half-sample is known exactly: it is a product of hypergeometric distributions.

Use that distribution to compute the deterministic correction $\Delta_n(k)
=
H_{2n}\!\left(\frac{k}{2n}\right)
-
\mathbb E\!\left[
H_n\!\left(\frac K n\right)\,\middle|\,k
\right].$ 

The second term is a finite classical calculation. It does not require more source experiments.

I obtained the uniform bound $\boxed{
\|\Delta_n(k)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le \frac{C}{n^2},
\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{out}}\Delta_n(k)=0.
}$ 

The proof uses half-sample symmetry to cancel odd Taylor terms, the exact hypergeometric variance, and fourth-derivative bounds. The bound holds for every possible count vector, which is what allows a physicality guarantee.

Make every correction executable

Set  $J_0=I/d^2$ , choose dyadic levels  $n_j=2^j n_0$ , and choose known probabilities $w_j=\frac{A}{n_j^2},
\qquad
S=\sum_jw_j.$ 

The constants are chosen so the following matrices remain positive: $J_{\mathrm{base}}
=
\frac{H_{n_0}-S J_0}{1-S},
\qquad
J_j
=
J_0+\frac{\Delta_{n_j}}{w_j}.$ 

Select the base branch with probability  $1-S$ , or correction level  $j$  with probability  $w_j$ . Every selected matrix is a normalized CPTP channel. No signed quantum operation is executed.

If $b_n(p)=\mathbb E_p H_n(\widehat p_n),$ 

then hypergeometric conditioning gives $\mathbb E_p\Delta_n=b_{2n}(p)-b_n(p).$ 

Consequently, $\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_p J_{\mathrm{program}}
&=
b_{n_0}(p)
+
\sum_{j\ge0}
\left[b_{2n_j}(p)-b_{n_j}(p)\right]\\
&=F(p).
\end{aligned}$ 

This establishes equality of the complete channel, including its action on an entangled payload.

Resources and synthesis

The acquisition terminates almost surely, with $\mathbb E T
\le
m n_0+\frac{4mA}{n_0}.$ 

Its displayed tail is polynomial,  $O(t^{-2})$ . The earlier exponential-tail complexity law has not been transferred to this construction.

I also removed a potentially hidden synthesis assumption. The construction can use a finite supplied catalogue consisting of:

At most  $(n_0+1)^m$  base channels.

 $2(d^4-d^2)+1$  fixed channels around the depolarizing channel, whose known mixtures implement all correction branches.

Thus arbitrary on-demand channel synthesis is unnecessary for the existence theorem. The catalogue can nevertheless be enormous. This replaces the general polytope/Wachspress preprocessing with an explicit grid and local directions; it does not establish efficient storage.

There is an important computational limitation: directly computing a correction can require  $(n+1)^m$  terms. Finite expected source calls do not establish finite expected total classical computation under this particular schedule.

Applying the theorem to Petz recovery

I constructed a smooth physical extension of affine tomography by clipping unphysical Choi eigenvalues and restoring the trace-preserving marginal. It agrees with the source throughout the promised floor class.

Bounded debiasing itself has a direct predecessor. Koskela, Karvonen, Łatuszyński and Spanò construct bounded scalar unbiased estimators using a random sample count independent of the observations. Their work must be credited. The contribution investigated here is the explicit positive matrix construction and its physical recovery-channel application; I am not claiming to have invented bounded debiasing or nonadaptive Bernoulli factories. arxiv.org

Exact scope

Acquisition measures each source output separately, with adaptive choices permitted. It may stop at an unbounded, almost-surely finite time. Only classical information survives acquisition.

Execution can be much more general:

Programs can be correlated across the batch.

Their conditional outputs can be entangled.

Exact reproduction is required on the entire promised channel class. The proof does not establish the same bound for approximate reproduction or collective quantum acquisition.

Replacer channels suffice: $\mathcal E_\rho(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(X)\rho,
\qquad
\rho\succeq \nu I/d.$ 

Every acquisition call supplies one copy of  $\rho$ . A classical record  $V$  must subsequently prepare states  $\sigma_V$  satisfying $\mathbb E_\rho[\sigma_V]=\rho^{\otimes M}.$ 

Two established information constraints meet here. The Gill–Massar bound limits the information obtainable from separately measured copies. Matsumoto’s reverse-estimation framework constrains the classical information needed to prepare a quantum statistical family. These are direct predecessors of the argument. arxiv.org+1

1+\frac{1}{d-1}

M\,\frac{2^n}{\nu}$

for every positive-probability finite stopping count.

finite-query exactness is a polynomial identity. Expanding acquisition into positive mixtures of unitary and depolarizing source slots, the first nonzero coefficient would have to prepare precisely the unknown unitary. A common depolarizing reference measure then rules out the required uncountably many disjoint successful classical identifications.

Finite random padding does not repair this exact conditional contract.

Full rank alone is insufficient for the obstruction. A known nonorthogonal random-unitary simplex admits a timing-neutral exact sampler, constructed in the accompanying notes. The universal family’s geometry matters.

Timing visibility does not automatically imply an  $\epsilon^{-2}$  cost. That estimation-type cost belongs to revealing the complete executable instruction. A hidden instruction with a fixed public acquisition cap can still be approximately correct under the earlier truncation contract.

The new debiasing construction illustrates the distinction particularly clearly: its acquisition length is selected before observing data, so its distribution reveals nothing about the unknown parameter. I completed a conditional bridge from the protected physical operations to conventional coherent fault correction—including repairs that read returning memory after a source becomes damaged. The decisive change was to use a representation in which individual fault amplitudes need not be normalized physical operations.

The construction

Fix each physical source’s decomposition into its logical qubit and its remaining gauge degrees of freedom. Keep those gauges, retired sources, controllers, records and returning environments in the complete memory. The clean-sector contribution to a location then has the form $G_j=U_j\otimes T_j,\qquad \|T_j\|\le 1.$ 

Here  $U_j$  is the intended logical gate.  $T_j$  may be a strict contraction. The actual operation remains an isometry; its residual  $B_j=W_j-G_j$  acts only on the location’s active logical wires and complete memory.

This matters because a perfectly acquired repair can still import memory information on a damaged input. In the new representation, that action remains a fault amplitude at the repair’s actual location. The earlier normalized causal counterexample remains valid: no later interaction has been deleted or moved backward.

Conventional fault-tolerance theory already supplies the Pauli-linearity and inclusion–exclusion machinery for handling such nonphysical amplitudes. I used that machinery directly. The new bridge establishes how our physical restoration theorem supplies its local support and complete marked-set bounds, without imposing a source-only decoder on every repair. arxiv.org+1

Given one common coherent outer decoder that corrects the declared benign fault paths, the construction aggregates the remaining bad amplitude into a bound  $\epsilon$ . It then produces a normalized reference on the same complete output memory: $\left\|Z-U_{\mathrm{target}}\otimes V\right\|\le 2\epsilon.$ 

I also derived the conditional recursion for disjoint groups of correctable operations. It preserves the original initialized, circuit-wide fault bound throughout; it does not insert fresh-bath assumptions at intermediate boundaries.

The full derivation is in    CONTRACTIVE_FAULT_BRIDGE.md.

A concrete corrected operation

The complementary construction uses the standard five-qubit code. A repair transmits a clean constituent identically, but on a dirty input lets returning memory select a single-site Pauli error. It resets the fresh gauge while retaining the old gauge and memory.

An explicit coherent decoder restores the logical input and moves the memory dependence into retained syndrome. This holds as an operator identity, including arbitrary initial reference and memory correlations. The helper’s 6,208 exact rational checks passed. Its two-site negative also passed:  $XXIII$  leaves a logical  $-Z$ , exposing the boundary of the correction rather than hiding it.

My separate exact checker passed the noncommuting-memory path identities, Boolean aggregation and a restricted-error coherent recovery construction. The new theorem passed scoped independent analytic review; the executed checkers remain separately identified author evidence.

What this makes possible—and what remains assumed

We now have a route for applying conventional coherent error correction to the retained-memory architecture without first making every inner repair independent of returning memory. The stronger source-only decoder construction remains available where its physical coupling conditions and better linear comparison are advantageous.

The computational bridge still requires an actual schedule with the stated local fault bounds and an outer correction implementation satisfying the operator identities. Preparation, controller acquisition, holding, noisy syndrome extraction, readout and reuse remain physical costs. A record that controls a logical choice must appear in the intended circuit with its errors charged; it cannot be made harmless by naming it environment.

The final normalization above is for a fixed completed program. It does not replace the earlier causal reference across future logical choices. These norm bounds are neither device fault probabilities nor an acquired computing threshold.

The earlier causal completion, finite controls, decoder constructions, alternative exchange mechanism, corrections and useful failures remain preserved. Deterministic text projection of the normally displayed final, preserving its mathematical annotations. This is not an acquired original proof, implementation, or independent review document. Raw visible text and private formula DOM are preserved separately.

New opening: local stationary-state preparation and control

I developed a different operational target: prepare a local part of an unknown many-body stationary quantum state, and estimate its control gradient, using a finite random history of local operations.

The strongest new theoretical step is a geometry argument for one-dimensional chains. It lowers the sufficient reset condition from more than one half to more than one quarter, while retaining finite expected work, an exponential history tail, and finite gradient variance. I also executed two stochastic control experiments, including one at 30% reset, where the original branching argument fails.

There is a consequential limitation: short burn-in outperformed the exact method at the precision tested in both examples. The completed advance is a constructive, rigorously costed operation and a stronger applicability theorem. A practical advantage—and a civilisation-changing consequence—remains unestablished.

The earlier positive matrix debiasing, exact classical batch resource law, timing distinctions and structured alternatives remain intact.

1. The operation and its actual interface

Consider local updates on a known interaction graph: $\mathcal E_e(\theta)
=\alpha\,\mathcal R_e+(1-\alpha)\,\mathcal F_e(\theta).$ 

Here:

 $\mathcal R_e$  completely resets the sites in edge  $e$ , removing their previous correlations.

 $\mathcal F_e(\theta)$  is a separately executable, memoryless local channel. It may be unknown, nonunital and entangling.

The experimenter generates the reset coin externally and can select the local update.

For gradients, the required shifted controls must be physically executable.

This changes the acquisition contract. The primary construction uses live local quantum-channel access. A mathematical decomposition of an unlabelled noisy channel does not supply its reset flag or its residual channel.

That distinction determined the direction. The supplied Uhlmann lead confirms that sample-access algorithms and physical Petz applications already exist; generic physical Petz implementation is therefore not the new destination. Its advertised low-rank regime also cannot simply be imported into the original globally faithful Choi class. arxiv.org

How the finite history works

Start from the sites whose stationary state or observable is wanted. Trace dependencies backward:

Select the next update touching the active set, with the correct incident-edge probability.

If it is a reset, remove that edge’s sites from the active set.

If it is a forward-channel update, add the entire edge to the active set.

Stop when the active set is empty. Reverse the recorded history and execute that finite circuit.

This works at the level of the full Heisenberg operator algebra. A reset eliminates dependence on its previous inputs even when those inputs are entangled. Once every backward dependency has disappeared, the requested output is independent of the arbitrary initial state.

Averaging these finite histories gives the stationary marginal. No global density matrix, channel tomography or chosen burn-in horizon is required.

2. The central new calculation: count clusters as well as sites

A generic  $b$ -site branching bound gives finite work when $b(1-\alpha)<1.$ 

For pair updates, this requires  $\alpha>1/2$ .

I found a stronger potential for uniformly updated nearest-neighbor paths. Let  $A$  be the active set and  $C(A)$  its number of connected runs. Define $W(A)=|A|+\frac{C(A)}{2\alpha},
\qquad
g=2\alpha-\frac12.$ 

The key inequality is $\mathbb E[\Delta W\mid A]\le -g.$ 

It holds throughout $\boxed{\alpha>\frac14.}$ 

The reason is geometric: resets can split a run, remove a short run completely, or erase its endpoints. Counting only occupied sites loses that information.

On the infinite path, an especially compact identity is $\mathcal LW
=-g\bigl(|A|+C(A)\bigr)
-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}G_1(A),$ 

where  $G_1(A)$  counts single-site gaps between runs. Filling those gaps merges runs and supplies the additional negative term.

For  $K$ , the number of relevant events before extinction, $\boxed{\mathbb E K\le \frac{W(A_0)}{g}.}$ 

Writing  $w=1/(2\alpha)$ , the audit also established $\mathbb E K^2
\le
\frac{W_0^2}{g^2}
+
\frac{\bigl((2+w)^2-g^2\bigr)W_0}{g^3},$ 

and, for  $t\ge W_0/g$ , $\Pr(K>t)
\le
\exp\!\left[
-\frac{2(gt-W_0)^2}{t(3+w)^2}
\right].$ 

These bounds depend on the requested region and reset gap, not the total chain length.

The independent audit verified the cluster calculation and finite endpoints. Its exact enumeration checked all nonempty active subsets on paths of sizes  $2,\ldots,12$ , covering the entire reset interval symbolically: 16,354 drift inequalities and 524,296 increment-range checks, with no violation. The analytic argument supplies the theorem; the enumeration corroborates it.

This is a sufficient threshold, not the critical point. Equal edge weights are substantive. The underlying stochastic process is also established: it is Sturm–Swart’s contact process with double deaths after time rescaling. Targeted research did not locate this precise one-quarter extinction bound, but comprehensive priority review remains open. stochastik.math.uni-goettingen.de

3. Turning preparation into an unbiased control operation

Suppose a local control has a valid physical shift identity $\partial_\theta\mathcal F_\theta
=c\bigl(\mathcal F_{\theta,+}-\mathcal F_{\theta,-}\bigr).$ 

For a Pauli rotation surrounded by parameter-independent noise,  $c=1/2$  and the shifts are  $\pm\pi/2$ .

For a sampled history with  $J$  eligible occurrences:

Select one eligible occurrence uniformly.

Select a sign  $s\in\{-1,+1\}$  uniformly.

Shift only that occurrence.

Execute the finite circuit and measure the desired norm-one observable, obtaining  $X\in[-1,1]$ .

Return $\widehat G=2cJsX.$ 

Then $\mathbb E\widehat G
=\partial_\theta\operatorname{Tr}[O\rho_{\rm ss}(\theta)].$ 

The history distribution is independent of the gate parameter. Its finite moments justify differentiating through the random stopping time and bound the estimator’s variance. Fresh histories preserve unbiasedness conditional on previous optimization decisions.

The finite-circuit stochastic-shift estimator has strong predecessors, and classical perfect sampling has already been combined with unbiased stationary derivatives. The investigated contribution is the local stationary quantum representation with explicit work and variance bounds, including the stronger path regime—not the invention of stochastic gradients. arxiv.org+1

What is actually saved in resources

For a fixed local objective and reset gap, the method has finite expected:

Relevant local channel and reset operations.

Classical history-generation work.

Visited quantum sites.

Gradient second moment.

Address bits, routing, gate durations and measurement costs remain. A fixed lattice still contains its physical hardware. Exact histories have unbounded tails; a fixed history or workspace cap gives a controlled approximation.

Separate local samples also do not provide adaptive access to one shared global quantum sample. Conditional on the current history, the output generally differs from the stationary marginal. The earlier timing and record distinctions remain applicable.

4. Executed control below the old threshold

The second benchmark uses three qubits, equal edge rates and  $\alpha=0.3$ : $\mathcal F_{12,\theta}
=0.9\,\mathcal B_\theta
+0.1\,\operatorname{Ad}_{CZ_{12}},
\qquad
\mathcal F_{23}=\operatorname{Ad}_{CZ_{23}},$ 

where  $\mathcal B_\theta$  prepares $|\Phi_\theta\rangle
=\frac{|00\rangle+e^{i\theta}|11\rangle}{\sqrt2}.$ 

These are directly executable residual operations. Their overlapping updates do not commute, and the stationary state retains pair entanglement.

I derived a closed stationary solution, independently verified against the channel equations. In particular, $\langle X_1X_2\rangle_{\rm ss}
=\frac{13041}{37949}\cos\theta.$ 

The pair marginal has partial-transpose eigenvalue $-\frac{155191}{3111818}\approx-0.0498715,$ 

certifying entanglement.

Stationary gradient experiment

At  $\theta=\pi/4$ , the exact derivative is  $-0.242994006$ .

 | Quantity | Executed result

 | Sampled histories | 30,000

 | Physical gradient estimate |  $-0.216667$ 

 | Standard error |  $0.029291$ 

 | Mean relevant events |  $8.9591$ 

 | Mean residual-channel invocations |  $6.2806$ 

 | Largest observed history | 94 events

 | Objective and gradient source invocations | 372,684

The gradient estimate is approximately  $0.90$  standard errors from its exact value. This is numerical consistency, not a replacement for the unbiasedness proof.

A separate seven-state absorbing-chain calculation gives the exact mean history length  $80/9$ , consistent with the simulation.

Actual stochastic optimization

Using only Born-valued gradient samples, twelve batches of 1,024 histories moved $\theta:1.2\longrightarrow0.120542.$ 

The exact objective diagnostics improved from $0.124523\longrightarrow0.341152,$ 

against the benchmark maximum  $0.343645$ . These exact diagnostics were not supplied to the optimizer.

Training consumed 73,954 simulated source invocations. Independent held-out evaluation consumed another 35,850, yielding objective  $0.3480$  with standard error  $0.01210$ . The complete second experiment used 482,488 simulated source invocations. These are synthetic local-channel calls, not hardware or fault-tolerant gate counts.

The full record is in   path_stationary_control_results.json.

5. The useful failure: burn-in remains the stronger practical baseline here

The comparison materially limits the claim.

 | Gradient method on the 30% reset benchmark | Bias | Expected source calls | Variance

 | Exact finite-history estimator | 0 | 6.0794 | 25.3049

 | Four-update burn-in |  $0.0033674$  | 2.4155 | 2.8126

 | Eight-update burn-in |  $0.0000546$  | 5.4627 | 9.6010

At the tested precision, short burn-in is more economical. The first, 55% reset experiment reached the same conclusion.

I also preserved a complementary size-biased-history estimator. It bounds the output amplitude by spending more work on longer genealogies; the executed one-qubit comparison showed a variance/work exchange, not a total-work improvement.

These failures matter. Removing bias is useful when the truncation error must be controlled rigorously, but exactness alone has not yet bought better control per source call.

6. What survived the primary-source comparison

The mechanism has substantial foundations:

Classical backward-ancestor perfect sampling already uses resets, reverse clocks, extinction and forward reconstruction. arxiv.org

Quantum coupling from the past already exists, including França’s Gibbs-state construction with spectral access. arxiv.org

High-noise local quantum dynamics already has strong classical simulation results based on spacetime percolation. arxiv.org

The exact double-death ancestry process and stochastic derivative ingredients are prior art.

The potentially distinctive completed object is therefore narrower: a physical local stationary-state and control operation for arbitrary noncommuting local channels, with an explicit executable interface, finite work and variance, and the one-quarter path criterion. Its priority and external proof acceptance remain open.

The competing quantum-memory routes are preserved too. Known Schur compression can retain identical samples compactly, while sample-based Hamiltonian simulation gives a sharp reminder that quantum retention does not guarantee linear batch throughput: its established time- $T$  cost is  $\Theta(T^2/\epsilon)$  in the stated regime. arxiv.org+1

Saved proofs and runnable work

   reset_ancestor_control.md — central construction and scope.

# Does ramification port a modular tensor algorithm to characteristic zero?

2026-10-30. This was a constructive attempt to replace an unsuccessful
ordinary lift by a genuinely different coefficient operation. The intended
capability was repeatable acquisition of characteristic-zero bilinear
algorithms from modular discoveries. The new mechanism was to admit
ramification (for example adjoining a square root of 2), not to repeat a
plus/flip search or a mod-4 test.

The attempt reaches a decisive failure for the acquired published seed.
The result below excludes **every finite ramification with this integral
reduction**, and explains which additional infinitesimal freedom would have
been needed. It does not exclude another reduction, coefficients with bad
reduction, or a characteristic-zero rank-47 algorithm globally.

## 1. The operation that ordinary lifting leaves unpaid

Let

`F(f)=sum_(r=1)^R a_r tensor b_r tensor c_r`

and let `T` be an integer target tensor. At an exact binary decomposition
`f0`, choose its 0/1 integer representative `fbar` and define

`J=dF(f0)`, `E=(T-F(fbar))/2 mod2`.

The familiar unrestricted mod-4 lift exists exactly when `E in im J`.
This is an established Hensel step, not the proposed new operation.

To see why this alone does not settle ramification, set `pi^2=2` and write
`f=fbar+pi x+pi^2 y (mod pi^3)`. The first two conditions are

`Jx=0`, `Jy+Q(x)=E`,

where `Q(x)` is the sum over terms of

`da tensor db tensor c + da tensor b tensor dc
                          + a tensor db tensor dc`.

A nongauge vector in `ker J` could therefore change the ordinary obstruction
through `Q(x)`. Failure of the ordinary linear step is not, by itself, a
proof that this quadratic problem fails. No such shortcut is used here.

The distinction is real even for the elementary equation `x^2=2`: its
binary point `x=0` has zero Jacobian and no mod-4 lift, but has the exact
ramified lift `x=sqrt(2)`. The tangent-spanning hypothesis paid below is
what excludes this possibility for the acquired tensor point.

We acquired the WHOLE kernel and tested whether it contains any direction
beyond exact symmetries. For the native input it does not. The next lemma
shows why that removes all ramification, not just this quadratic ansatz.

## 2. Gauge-complete tangent lemma

The lemma is stated for any prime `p`, any integer polynomial system
`F(f)=T`, and a point `f0` over `F_p`. Suppose there is a finite collection
of transformations defined over `Z_(p)`, with denominators invertible near
their identity, having the following properties:

1. Each transformation is the identity at parameter zero.
2. It preserves the solution set `F(f)=T`, and every congruence version of
   that equation. Equivariance with an invertible target representation
   fixing `T` suffices; `F` itself need not be pointwise invariant.
3. Their tangent vectors at `f0` span ALL of `ker dF(f0)`.

Let `fs` be ANY integral tuple with reduction `f0` such that
`F(fs)=T (mod p^s)`. Put

`Es=(T-F(fs))/p^s mod p`.

**Lemma.** If `Es` is outside `im J`, then there is no solution over any
mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring `R` with residue characteristic
`p`, finite `e=v_R(p)`, and reduction `f0`. In fact a solution is impossible
already modulo `pi^(es+1)`, where `pi` is a uniformizer. The conclusion
holds after ANY residue field extension.

**Proof.** Work in `R/(pi^(es+1))`, where `p=u pi^e` with `u` a unit.
Suppose there is a solution `f`. We successively apply the exact
transformations to make

`f=fs (mod pi^k)`

for `k=1,...,es`. The first assertion holds by the common reduction.
If `k<es` and the assertion holds at `k`, write
`f=fs+pi^k x (mod pi^(k+1))`. Polynomial expansion and `2k>=k+1` give

`F(f)=F(fs)+pi^k Jx (mod pi^(k+1))`.

Since `F(fs)-T` is divisible by `pi^(es)` and `k+1<=es`, `Jx=0` in the
residue field. The tangent-spanning premise remains true over that field:
it is a rank equality for finite matrices over `F_p`. Choose a linear
combination of the supplied tangent generators equal to `-x`.

Lift these finitely many residue coefficients to `R` and compose the exact
transformations with parameters `pi^k` times those lifts. Their leading
effect is `-pi^k x`; products of two such perturbations occur only at order
`pi^(2k)>=pi^(k+1)`. Their denominators are units. The transformed tuple is
still a solution and now agrees with `fs` modulo `pi^(k+1)`.

After finitely many such corrections,
`f=fs+pi^(es) y (mod pi^(es+1))`. At this last order the equation requires

`Jy=u^s Es`

in the residue field (up to the harmless consistent sign convention).
The right side is a nonzero scalar multiple of a vector outside `im J`,
which is impossible. Inconsistency of a linear system over `F_p` persists
over every field extension. This proves the lemma. No completeness,
convergence, norm, or unbounded iterative-limit premise was used. End proof.

**Consequence for a positive porting algorithm.** Under the same tangent
premise, a ramified lift can never rescue ANY failed ordinary Hensel step.
If a mixed-characteristic solution with this reduction exists, every
ordinary step from every already acquired integral approximation is
solvable. Differences between solutions of a step lie in the gauge tangent
and can be removed by the supplied transformations at that order. Thus
branching into coefficient extensions is not new existence leverage at a
gauge-complete point. This is a formal local statement. It does not provide
a rational height bound, terminating rational reconstruction, or a complex
algorithm from an infinite p-adic series.

## 3. Exact symmetries for the acquired matrix tensor

The 4-by-4 target uses the cyclic coefficient convention

`T=sum_(i,j,k=0)^3 E_ij tensor E_jk tensor E_ki`.

For invertible four-by-four matrices `P,Q,R`, apply to every term

`a -> P a Q^-1`, `b -> Q b R^-1`, `c -> R c P^-1`.

The induced tensor representation fixes `T` over EVERY commutative ring:
the three sums contract `Q^-1 Q`, `R^-1 R`, and `P^-1 P` to identities.
These transformations preserve the solution set, not arbitrary represented
tensor values. For each term also use

`(a,b,c) -> (s a,t b,(s t)^-1 c)`

with unit `s,t`; this transformation does preserve the represented tensor
itself. All identity-near transformations are defined by finite matrix
inversion and unit division, valid in every ring used in the lemma.

Their tangent vectors, for arbitrary four-by-four `X,Y,Z`, are

`da=Xa-aY`, `db=Yb-bZ`, `dc=Zc-cX`,

and the two per-term scaling directions. At characteristic two minus equals
plus. There are `3*16+2*47=142` listed generators, with rank at most
`142-3=139` because the central matrix/scaling parameters are redundant.
We do not infer equality from this parameter count; it is acquired below.

## 4. Actual native computation

The input is the authors' published `factorizations_f2.npz`, key `4,4,4`,
shape `(3,16,47)`, SHA256
`70f09f349d8d2874ef0e0e089459c7320f5aa3eef277df5ffa67f573709db2da`.
Attribution: Fawzi et al., *Nature*610 (2022), the official Google DeepMind
AlphaTensor repository; nonsoftware materials are supplied under CC-BY4.0.
Its original source/license and prior acquisition are retained in the
read-only sol23 source receipt. This run reuses those acquired bytes.

`ramified_probe.py` is a new standalone exact GF(2) computation. It does not
import the previous tangent compiler. It reconstructs the integer tensor,
all 4,096 coefficient equations, every Jacobian column, the entire kernel,
and all the exact-symmetry tangent generators above. The parameter order is
term, mode, entry. Python integers encode exact binary vectors; NumPy is
used only for the finite integer arrays and tensor products/sums.

The acquired result is

| Quantity | Exact value |
| --- | ---: |
| Tensor coefficients | 4,096 |
| Factor parameters | 2,256 |
| Jacobian rank | 2,117 |
| Kernel dimension | 139 |
| Listed exact-symmetry generators | 142 |
| Their rank | 139 |
| Kernel basis vectors outside their span | 0 |

Every computed kernel vector and every symmetry generator is separately
checked to have zero Jacobian image. Kernel vectors are obtained from
tracked generating-column dependencies. Every one is reduced by the
symmetry basis. Thus all tangent directions are acquired and accounted for;
there is no unsearched nongauge subspace being set to zero by an ansatz.

The old mod-4 obstruction is recomputed. To expose a directly consumable
witness, the final run constructs a binary tensor functional `ell` and
checks all 2,256 identities

`ell(J_column)=0`, while `ell(E)=1`.

It has 255 nonzero entries. The explicit dual, kernel basis, symmetry
generators, and defect are in `RAMIFICATION_WITNESSES.json`; hashes alone
are not substituted for these mathematical witnesses.

The final exact run took `0.0328371 s` after imports. The first successful
run took `0.0349093 s`; it was retained, then repeated once specifically to
export the new dual obstruction witness. One preceding command failed
before reading the input because of an incorrectly resolved relative path;
that path was corrected. No new source case, random pool, tuning, or
nonlinear characteristic-zero search was run.

## 5. Decisive conclusion and exact exclusions

Apply the lemma at `p=2,s=1`. There is no integral rank-47 tensor
decomposition over ANY finite ramified extension of a mixed-characteristic
valuation ring reducing to the acquired binary seed. More strongly, if
`2=u pi^e`, it already fails modulo `pi^(e+1)`. In particular, adjoining
`sqrt(2)`, `i`, or higher finite ramification cannot repair this reduction.

The same conclusion holds for any residue-field extension and for a
reduction in the orbit of the displayed target-preserving matrix/unit
symmetries and term permutations: lift that invertible residue symmetry,
apply its inverse first, and use the lemma at the original seed.

The conclusion does NOT exclude:

* a different binary rank-47 decomposition outside this orbit;
* a characteristic-zero scheme with different/bad PROJECTIVE reduction;
* paths that change rank, global searches, or other components;
* a characteristic-zero rank-47 algorithm, a better large-matrix exponent,
  or practical matrix multiplication gains.

The concrete positive hypothesis was that ramification could activate a
quadratic repair hidden from the ordinary tangent image. At this seed every
available first-order deformation is gauge, so exact finite gauge removal
closes that hypothesis at EVERY finite ramification order. The general
criterion changes which modular points merit such a search: nongauge
infinitesimal directions are necessary for a genuinely ramified escape,
though they are not sufficient. No new characteristic-zero algorithm was
acquired. Continuing this same ramified seed search is not justified.

## 6. Individual coefficient poles are not a projective escape here

There is a second possible escape to check rather than silently assume
away: perhaps coefficients with even denominators approach the same binary
factor DIRECTIONS, with cancellations between divergent terms. That issue
is distinct from integral lifting.

**Projective lemma.** Suppose the reduced rank-one TERM tensors
`tr=ar tensor br tensor cr` of a modular decomposition are linearly
independent. Let a decomposition over the fraction field of a discrete
valuation ring have the same projective factor reductions, term by term.
Then unit and possibly nonunit per-term factor rescalings convert it to an
integral decomposition reducing to the original modular decomposition.

**Proof.** Normalize each factor separately to a primitive integral vector
whose nonzero reduction is exactly its prescribed modular factor. A term
then has the form `kr ar_tilde tensor br_tilde tensor cr_tilde`, with
arbitrary nonzero coefficient `kr` in the fraction field. If the smallest
valuation `w` among the `kr` is negative, multiply the tensor equation by
`pi^(-w)` and reduce. The integral target disappears; the nonzero unit
residues of those `kr` attaining the minimum give a nontrivial linear
dependence among the corresponding `tr`. This contradicts independence.
Thus all term valuations are nonnegative.

Reduce the original equation. Its target is `sum_r tr`. Independence makes
this coefficient representation unique. Every term must consequently have
valuation zero and coefficient residue one. Absorb each unit `kr` into its
third primitive factor. The resulting integral tuple reduces exactly to
the given modular decomposition and represents the same target. End proof.

`projective_probe.py` acquires the new native premise, without repeating
the Jacobian search: the 47 term tensors have binary column rank47. The
script exports all term columns and pivot rows in `PROJECTIVE_PROBE.json`.
This additional exact run took0.00604351s after imports.

Combining the two lemmas therefore rules out even a fraction-field
decomposition with poles in individual factors whose PROJECTIVE factors
specialize to this native point (or to its stated symmetry orbit). Merely
allowing `1/2` coefficients while keeping these projective limiting factors
cannot evade the failure. A target-preserving fraction-field isotropy may
also be applied first: if its transformed factors had this specialization,
they would be forbidden by the same argument.

This still does not exclude bad-reduction boundary configurations with
linearly DEPENDENT limiting term tensors, or different modular algorithm
points. Such dependence allows cancellation of leading poles; it is an
actual missing representation for a new search, not a resource supplied by
the native array. The projective statement is valuative in characteristic
two, not a statement about a Euclidean neighborhood of complex algorithms.

PROOF gives an exact conductance draw. Its conditional field distribution is a
normalized Gaussian and must be paid, not treated as the already executed output.
The sibling quantized_field.py implements this completion using outward Arb.

For the rational positive-definite covariance C=L_x^(-1), an exact rational LDL
factorization gives C=T D T^T, with T unit lower triangular and D strictly positive.
Fresh independent Box--Muller pairs

    Z_1=sqrt(-2 log U) cos(2 pi V),
    Z_2=sqrt(-2 log U) sin(2 pi V)

give the required independent real normals. Each field component is T sqrt(D) Z.
The output is the componentwise floor on a SUPPLIED positive rational grid width.
It is the normalized full field law pushed through this quantizer, with the pinned
site omitted. It is not an exact finite string representing a continuous real.

Every U,V is a persistent lazy fair-bit interval. Increase its precision and use
outward elementary functions and arithmetic until every floor is unique. No
floating midpoint, accepted tolerance, Gaussian cutoff, or resampling of ambiguous
fields governs the result. The executable pseudorandom source is diagnostic only;
the probabilistic theorem assumes iid fair bits and correct outward operations.

For a fixed finite input, termination and finite expected requested precision can
be justified without assuming independent adaptive precisions. At depth p, exclude
U outside [2^(-p/3),1-2^(-p/3)] for ALL radial uniforms. This event has probability
O(nr 2^(-p/3)). On the complement the Box--Muller map has a deterministic derivative
bound growing at most O(poly(p) 2^(p/2)); input intervals of width 2^-p therefore
give exponentially shrinking field intervals, after charging the finite LDL norm.
Working precision can be enlarged to pay elementary rounding as well.

For each nonzero-variance marginal Gaussian X and fixed grid width delta, the
wrapped density sum sum_k f_X(k delta) is finite (and bounded, for example, by
1/delta+2 sup f_X). Therefore the probability that an output coordinate lies within
w of ANY grid boundary is at most O(w(1/delta+sup f_X)), with a harmless enlargement
of the constant for w<delta/4. Union over finitely many coordinates proves an
exponentially decaying unresolved-depth tail. This argument is unconditional over
U,V and holds separately for every conductance state. There are finitely many such
states, so uniform finite constants exist; no independence between the requested
precision and the random output is presumed.

Thus the ideal elementary-interval algorithm has finite mean requested random bits
and finite mean elementary evaluation precision. Rational graph/determinant bounds
control the finite LDL coefficient sizes. This does NOT certify a general expected
CPU bit-complexity theorem for the installed python-flint/Arb implementation or
claim that dense LDL is the fastest Gaussian sampler. All field precision and
factorization operations are included in the actual execution receipt.

# Two localization calculations and the unresolved sequential step

30 October 2026. Root derivation. These are ordinary probability/convex
identities, not claimed historical novelties or a completed compiler.

1. Write d_t(h)=D(P_future|h || Q_future|h). Chain rule gives
E_(h~P[:t]) d_t(h)<=Delta for every cut. Therefore a fresh batch of N target
prefixes has d_t(h)<=kappa at EVERY sampled prefix except with probability
at most N Delta/kappa. Their conditional future vectors then differ in L1
by at most sqrt(2kappa). An arbitrary adaptively queried prefix has no such
guarantee. If one samples Q prefixes instead, a further N sqrt(Delta/2)
union allowance suffices by coupling prefix marginals. This is not a
conditional P oracle.

For a good prefix h and an extension o with P(o|h)>=tau, conditional chain
rule gives d_(t+1)(ho)<=kappa/tau. Teacher-heavy extensions can be related
to this premise using the next-token marginal TV bound. Repeating this
division through a chain may cost tau^(-T), which is not polynomial in T.

2. Let C be a convex subset of the finite probability simplex and let
z_star minimize D(z_prime||w) over C, with positive w,z_star. For every
z0 in C, the first-order projection inequality implies

    <z0,log(w/z_star)><=0.

For any target z, if ||z-z0||1<=e and the coordinatewise log ratio is
bounded in absolute value by B, then

    D(z||z_star)<=D(z||w)+e B.

Indeed the difference is <z,log(w/z_star)>; insert z0 and use the preceding
inequality. If w,z_star lie between a mu and b mu for the same dominating
positive measure mu, B=log(b/a). This removes the factor-two L1 projection
loss even under APPROXIMATE representability, at a paid log-ratio cost.
It does not grant a computable dominating measure, full-future positivity,
